chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Black Cat hours, John Hammond and the audition
summary: They played midnight to four; Hammond heard him there and set up the audition at the Roseland for Basie.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: There was something funny about that place, because '37 was the year I came.
Are we up to '37 already?
Yeah.
We've got to be.
How come?

Because, you know, I came with a friend of mine, from England and Then he fell in love with a hat-check girl who lived out on Long Island. And he had to go down to the Black Cat about four in the morning, you know --
That's right. That's what time we got through.
We'd go to work at twelve o'clock at night.
Yeah.
And we got through at four o'clock in the morning.
Well, he'd take her way out to Long Island, then come back to the Lincoln Hotel where we were staying, get home about eight.
That's right.
Well, that's right, because the Yeah Man must have been how long?
But, lock no. Basie came to New York in '36.
Yeah, well, Freddie joined him in '37.
That's right. That's right. And, I was at the Black Cat doing that thing, because I had to leave the Black Cat and make
an audition at the Roseland Ballroom to join Basie's band.
You mean to say when Basie played the Roseland you were playing with him for the first time?
Yeah. Now that's not -- listen. In the Village, I worked at the Black Cat.
Yeah, right.
John Hammond used to come in there -- okay -- and hear me play and all that and he made the audition for me when Basie came to town, you know.
Basie didn't bring any guitar player?
He had a guitar player, Claude Williams. Yes. Guitar and violin.
Claude Williams.
And, I made the audition with him, and got the job, more or less. In the meantime, I had a recording date, my first recording date with Billie Holiday, during this period.
With Teddy, Buck Clayton, and Lester.
With Teddy?
This was John again?
Right.
What session was that, do you remember those titles?
We can look that up. Don't worry.
Well, I just wondered because --
Basie came in '36 didn't he?
Yeah.
Mm hmm.
